statements: Every stratum was decided from the Q field and the issue author's opening body in stratum-input.jsonl and from nothing else.

I opened exactly three files: the assignment brief, docs/eval/retrieval/dataset-v2-inclusion-rule.md, and docs/eval/retrieval/harvests/sw-279-phase-2a2/stratum-input.jsonl. I read Section 5 of the frozen rule verbatim rather than a paraphrase.
I opened no Cobra source, no graphi source, no test, and no dataset or judgement file, and I navigated no checkout.

I ran no search of any kind - no graphi CLI, no mcp__graphi__* tool, no semantic or lexical search, no grep or glob over the repository - and I saw no ranked result, score, bundle, or other retrieval output for any of these questions.
I made no GitHub, web, or connector request; no issue was looked up, and external links appearing as literal text in the bodies were not opened.
I used the shell only to write my two output files, to validate the output against the input row set, and to compute the three sha256 digests recorded above.
I applied rules 1, 2 and 3 in the frozen precedence order, taking the first applicable rule for each row, and I recorded that rule number alongside the stratum.

I did not balance the strata toward any count: no per-stratum target was used, and no assignment was influenced by where an answer might be found, how many answer spans might exist, or how a retriever might perform. The resulting distribution (90 config_docs, 3 nl_behaviour, 1 architecture_flow) is the unadjusted output of the precedence order applied row by row.
No question was assigned exact_identifier, exact_path, ambiguous, or no_hit.
